title: Posterior interosseous nerve injury at the supinator: finger/thumb extension weakness
vignette: A 35-year-old, right-handed mechanic comes to the clinic due to progressive right hand weakness. The patient frequently uses a screwdriver at work. Neurologic examination shows preserved sensation in the upper limbs. There is weakness on extension of the fingers and thumb in the right hand. Strength is otherwise intact. Triceps reflexes are 2+ and bilaterally symmetric. The nerve affected in this patient was most likely injured at which of the following locations?

clues.text: frequently uses a screwdriver at work
clues.note: Repetitive pronation/supination (screwdriver use) can compress the deep branch of the radial nerve (posterior interosseous nerve) as it passes through the supinator muscle.

clues.text: preserved sensation in the upper limbs
clues.note: PRESERVED sensation indicates the injured nerve is the deep MOTOR branch (posterior interosseous nerve) - which is purely motor - AFTER the sensory (superficial) branch has split off.

clues.text: weakness on extension of the fingers and thumb
clues.note: Weak FINGER and THUMB extension with intact wrist extension/triceps localizes to the posterior interosseous nerve (after branches to those muscles have left).

clues.text: Triceps reflexes are 2+ and bilaterally symmetric
clues.note: Intact triceps (elbow extension) reflex means the lesion is DISTAL to the triceps branches - i.e., in the forearm, not at the axilla/humerus.

whatMatters: Weak FINGER and THUMB extension with SPARED sensation, wrist extension, and triceps = injury to the POSTERIOR INTEROSSEOUS NERVE (the deep, purely-motor branch of the radial nerve) where it passes through the SUPINATOR MUSCLE. Answer F. (Repetitive pronation/supination, e.g., screwdriver use, is the cause.)
strategy: Localize the radial nerve lesion by what is SPARED. Preserved sensation + intact triceps + intact wrist extension, but weak finger/thumb extension = the deep branch (posterior interosseous nerve) AFTER it passes the SUPINATOR. Reject the axilla and humeral midshaft (would cause wrist drop + sensory loss ± triceps weakness), carpal tunnel and hook of hamate (median/ulnar at the wrist), and coracobrachialis (musculocutaneous nerve region).

eliminations.label: Axilla - would cause wrist drop + sensory loss + weak triceps
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: radial nerve injury at the axilla (e.g., 'crutch palsy'). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: a proximal lesion causes WRIST DROP (weak wrist AND finger extension), sensory loss over the posterior arm/dorsal hand, and often weak elbow extension - this patient has intact sensation, wrist extension, and triceps. ✅ Correct if: wrist drop + sensory loss + triceps weakness (proximal radial lesion).

eliminations.label: Carpal tunnel - median nerve at the wrist
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: median nerve compression at the wrist (carpal tunnel syndrome). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it causes thenar weakness and median sensory symptoms, not finger/thumb EXTENSION weakness (a radial/posterior interosseous function). ✅ Correct if: thenar weakness + median sensory loss.

eliminations.label: Coracobrachialis - musculocutaneous nerve
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: the coracobrachialis is pierced by the musculocutaneous nerve (elbow flexion/forearm sensation). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it is unrelated to finger/thumb extension (a radial function). ✅ Correct if: weak elbow flexion + lateral forearm sensory loss (musculocutaneous).

eliminations.label: Hook of hamate - ulnar nerve at the wrist (your pick)
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: the ulnar nerve passes near the hook of hamate (Guyon canal). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: ulnar injury causes weak finger abduction/adduction and 4th-5th digit sensory loss - not finger/thumb EXTENSION weakness with preserved sensation. ✅ Correct if: ulnar claw/hypothenar findings.

eliminations.label: Midshaft of the humerus - wrist drop + sensory loss
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: radial nerve in the spiral (radial) groove (midshaft humeral fracture, 'Saturday night palsy'). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it causes WRIST DROP (weak wrist and finger extension) plus dorsal-hand sensory loss (triceps usually spared) - this patient's wrist extension and sensation are intact. ✅ Correct if: wrist drop with sensory loss, triceps spared (midshaft humerus).

reasoning: Weak finger/thumb extension but INTACT sensation, wrist extension, and triceps
This localizes to the deep, purely-motor branch of the radial nerve (posterior interosseous nerve)
The posterior interosseous nerve is entrapped as it passes through the SUPINATOR muscle (repetitive pronation/supination)
mechanism: The RADIAL nerve enters the forearm anterior to the lateral epicondyle and divides into a SUPERFICIAL (purely SENSORY) branch and a DEEP (purely MOTOR) branch. The deep branch passes BETWEEN the two heads of the SUPINATOR muscle and continues as the POSTERIOR INTEROSSEOUS NERVE, innervating the finger and thumb extensors (and other deep extensors). Because the branches to the triceps (elbow extension) and to the extensor carpi radialis longus (a wrist extensor) leave PROXIMAL to the supinator, injury to the deep branch AT the supinator (from repetitive pronation/supination, e.g., screwdriver use, or trauma/radial head dislocation) causes weakness of FINGER and THUMB extension ('finger drop') while SPARING the triceps reflex, wrist extension, and - critically - all SENSATION (the sensory branch has already separated). This localizes the lesion to the supinator. Contrast a proximal radial nerve lesion at the AXILLA or MIDSHAFT HUMERUS, which causes 'wrist drop' (weak wrist AND finger extension) with dorsal-hand sensory loss (and, at the axilla, weak triceps).

difficulty.label: 🧠 Knowledge
difficulty.text: First Aid Anatomy > radial nerve branches: superficial (sensory) + deep (motor -> posterior interosseous nerve through supinator); PIN injury = finger/thumb extension weakness, no sensory loss, triceps/wrist extension spared; proximal lesions = wrist drop + sensory loss.

difficulty.label: 📖 Comprehension
difficulty.text: Preserved sensation + intact triceps/wrist extension + finger drop = posterior interosseous nerve at the supinator.

difficulty.label: 🔤 Vocab
difficulty.text: Unsure on posterior interosseous nerve, deep vs superficial radial branch, supinator, finger drop vs wrist drop? Tell me which.

difficulty.label: 🨤 Distractor
difficulty.text: Axilla/midshaft humerus = wrist drop + sensory loss; carpal tunnel (median), hook of hamate (ulnar), coracobrachialis (musculocutaneous).

difficulty.label: 🗒️ Other
difficulty.text: Bank: posterior interosseous nerve (deep radial) at supinator -> finger/thumb extension weakness, NO sensory loss, wrist extension/triceps spared.

keywords.front: Finger/thumb extension weakness, sensation intact, wrist extension spared
keywords.back: Posterior interosseous nerve at the supinator

keywords.front: Radial nerve branches in the forearm
Posterior interosseous vs proximal radial lesion
keywords.back: Finger drop (no sensory loss) vs wrist drop (+ sensory loss)
Wrist drop + dorsal-hand sensory loss (triceps spared)

firstAid.detail: Anatomy: deep radial branch through supinator; finger/thumb extension, no sensory loss.
Anatomy > axilla/midshaft (wrist drop + sensory), carpal tunnel (median), hamate (ulnar).
Anatomy > repetitive pronation/supination (screwdriver), radial head trauma.

memoryHook: Deep radial branch dives through the supinator and becomes the posterior interosseous - a pure motor nerve; pinch it and the fingers/thumb won't extend, but sensation, wrist, and triceps are fine (finger drop, not wrist drop).
